01 / ORIENTATION

Understand the layer before the label.

A UI library, a server framework and a runtime solve different problems. This directory preserves all 631 technologies in the supplied research pack dated 23 September 2026, including historical entries. Inclusion does not establish current maintenance or suitability for a new project.

Different measures. Different questions.

Developer-reported use, survey satisfaction and detected website deployments have different denominators. Imported numerical snapshots are attributed to the supplied pack and have not all been independently revalidated. They are not one universal market-share ranking.

02 / ARCHITECTURE

Where does the technology fit?

Library, framework, runtime, CMS or generator?

A library supplies building blocks that your code calls. A framework supplies conventions and often controls request or rendering flow. A runtime executes code and exposes platform APIs. A CMS manages content and editorial workflows. A static-site generator builds deployable pages ahead of requests. These roles can overlap; the catalogue retains its original classification alongside the technical guides.

React is a UI library; Node.js is a runtime; WordPress is a CMS. Treating all three as interchangeable framework choices hides the actual architectural decision.

Client, server and full-stack boundaries

Client code runs in an environment controlled by the user. It can improve interaction but cannot be trusted to authorize sensitive operations. Server code validates requests, checks permissions and accesses protected services. Full-stack tools connect these environments; they do not remove the boundary between them.

Rendering: CSR, SSR, static generation and hydration

Client-side rendering creates views in the browser. Server-side rendering produces HTML during request handling. Static generation produces it during a build. Hydration attaches client behavior to existing HTML; islands limit that behavior to selected components. Consider cacheability, freshness, accessibility and transferred JavaScript, not just initial appearance.

The request lifecycle

A typical server request passes through routing, middleware, authentication, authorization, validation and application logic before producing a response. Database transactions, timeouts and error mapping belong in that design. Background jobs need retries, idempotency and observability; successful queue submission does not mean the job succeeded.

How to evaluate a framework
  1. Define deployment targets, team knowledge and the product’s data boundaries.
  2. Prototype an awkward real workflow, including failures and permissions.
  3. Measure representative page weight, latency and database queries.
  4. Check official support policies, upgrade paths and dependency maintenance.
  5. Document migrations, backups, logging and recovery responsibilities.

Use the research tables as context. Before choosing a dependency, review its current primary documentation and release history.

03 / TECHNICAL FIELD GUIDES

Roles, mechanics and tradeoffs.

These 12 editorial guides describe typical engineering work, not measured occupational or demographic shares. The complete imported catalogue follows.

ReactUI library / browser

Role & typical users

Frontend developers use React to compose interactive interfaces from reusable components.

Technical model

Components express output from props and state. Events update state; the UI is rendered again. Routing and application-level data access require additional choices.

Engineering considerations

Keep state ownership explicit, use stable list keys and test keyboard behavior. Rendering a login screen does not implement server authorization.

Try building

Build a searchable list with loading, empty and error states.

Primary documentation ↗

AngularApplication framework / client

Role & typical users

Application teams use Angular for structured browser applications with integrated platform features.

Technical model

Components, templates, dependency injection and routing organize application behavior. TypeScript supports typed interfaces; reactive state helps update views.

Engineering considerations

Keep service boundaries clear and avoid turning every component into a global-state consumer. Budget browser bundles and test form accessibility.

Try building

Build a routed settings page with validation and an unsaved-changes state.

Primary documentation ↗

Vue.jsUI framework / client

Role & typical users

Frontend developers use Vue for incremental enhancement or complete component-based applications.

Technical model

Declarative templates and reactive state connect data to rendered UI. Single-file components can colocate template, behavior and styling.

Engineering considerations

Distinguish derived state from side effects. Choose routing, server rendering and data-fetching approaches to match the application.

Try building

Create a filterable catalogue with reusable item components.

Primary documentation ↗

Next.jsReact application framework / full-stack

Role & typical users

Web application teams use Next.js to combine React interfaces with routing and server-side application features.

Technical model

Server and client components divide work between environments. Rendering, data fetching and caching choices affect what ships to the browser.

Engineering considerations

Understand cache invalidation and the server/client boundary. Authenticate and authorize server operations; do not expose secrets through client bundles.

Try building

Build a read-only documentation route and compare static and request-time rendering.

Primary documentation ↗

Node.jsJavaScript runtime / server

Role & typical users

Backend and tooling developers use Node.js to run JavaScript outside a browser. It is a runtime, not a UI or application framework.

Technical model

The runtime supplies server APIs and asynchronous I/O. An event loop coordinates callbacks and tasks; CPU-heavy work can delay other requests.

Engineering considerations

Bound request sizes, use timeouts and move expensive work off the event loop where appropriate. A framework adds routing conventions above the runtime.

Try building

Create a small HTTP endpoint with explicit error responses.

Primary documentation ↗

ExpressHTTP framework / server

Role & typical users

Node.js backend developers use Express for HTTP routing and middleware pipelines.

Technical model

Requests pass through configured middleware and route handlers. The framework provides HTTP conveniences without prescribing an entire data architecture.

Engineering considerations

Middleware order matters. Validate input, centralize error responses and configure proxy trust deliberately for the actual deployment.

Try building

Build an API with validation, a not-found response and an error handler.

Primary documentation ↗

DjangoPython application framework / server

Role & typical users

Backend developers use Django for data-driven sites with models, routing, templates and administration.

Technical model

An object-relational mapper maps models to database operations. URL routing selects views; templates render output and migrations evolve schema.

Engineering considerations

Enforce authorization at the view and object level. Review query counts, migration behavior and deployment settings; an admin interface is not a public API.

Try building

Build a reading list with ownership checks and database constraints.

Primary documentation ↗

FastAPIPython API framework / server

Role & typical users

API developers use FastAPI for typed request contracts and generated API documentation.

Technical model

Python annotations describe inputs and outputs. Validation and OpenAPI generation support explicit contracts; async endpoints can cooperate during I/O waits.

Engineering considerations

A validated shape is not permission to act. Separate validation, authentication and authorization; avoid blocking calls inside async request paths.

Try building

Build a paginated API that validates limits and tests error payloads.

Primary documentation ↗

LaravelPHP application framework / server

Role & typical users

PHP application teams use Laravel for web products with common routing, database and application-service needs.

Technical model

Routing, dependency injection, Eloquent models, migrations and queues provide conventions around application work.

Engineering considerations

Use policies for authorization and validate input. Make background jobs idempotent and consider transactions before sending follow-up work.

Try building

Build a request workflow with a policy check and queued notification.

Primary documentation ↗

Ruby on RailsRuby application framework / server

Role & typical users

Product developers use Rails to build database-backed web applications around shared conventions.

Technical model

MVC separates models, views and controllers. Active Record and migrations organize relational persistence; routing connects requests to actions.

Engineering considerations

Keep authorization explicit and watch query volume. Use transactions and constraints for durable invariants rather than relying only on form validation.

Try building

Build a small issue tracker with per-user access and model tests.

Primary documentation ↗

AstroContent framework / build-time and server

Role & typical users

Documentation and content-site developers use Astro to deliver pages with selective interactivity.

Technical model

Islands architecture isolates interactive components while keeping the rest of the page focused on HTML. Rendering and deployment choices depend on the project.

Engineering considerations

Only hydrate components that need client behavior. Check content provenance, accessible navigation and the cost of third-party scripts.

Try building

Build a documentation site with one interactive search component.

Primary documentation ↗

WordPressContent management system / server

Role & typical users

Publishers, site administrators and developers use WordPress to manage content and extend sites through themes and plugins.

Technical model

The CMS supplies content workflows and extension points. Themes present content; plugins add functionality and may expand the application’s trust boundary.

Engineering considerations

Review plugin maintenance, user capabilities, updates and backups. Editorial access and administrative access should be distinct.

Try building

Model an editorial workflow with separate author and administrator capabilities.

Primary documentation ↗

07 / COVERAGE & LIMITATIONS

Read the methodology.

The catalogue is broad rather than exhaustive. Its source classifications are retained, including broad or combined type labels. Detailed guides clarify the tools they cover. Catalogue counts describe this pack, not market size.

Workbook overview

CODARIS Web Frameworks & Technologies Research Dataset

Metric · Value

Catalogue entries · 631

Stack Overflow 2025 ranked technologies · 26

Primary ecosystems · 29

Catalogue categories · 28

Country/region rows · 146

Research sources · 21

IMPORTANT: React is a library, Node.js/Deno/Bun are runtimes, WordPress/Drupal are CMS platforms, and CSS systems such as Tailwind/Bootstrap are styling frameworks. CODARIS should keep these types separate. The shared catalogue exists for discovery, not to claim every entry is the same kind of technology.

POPULARITY: Stack Overflow percentages describe survey respondents who reported extensive use in the prior year. State of JS percentages describe its JavaScript-community respondents. W3Techs measures detected technologies on websites. These metrics are not directly interchangeable and should never be averaged into a single universal usage percentage.

Methodology
Methodology
IssueCODARIS treatmentReason
Framework vs library vs runtimeKeep an explicit Type field. React is a library; Node.js/Deno/Bun are runtimes; WordPress/Drupal are CMS platforms.Developer surveys often group heterogeneous web technologies together, but educational pages should not erase technical distinctions.
Catalogue scopeBroad curated catalogue of 631 technologies gathered across major ecosystem comparison/awesome lists.There is no authoritative finite list of every web framework ever created. This is a researched educational catalogue, not a claim of total completeness.
Stack Overflow usageUse the 2025 'Have Used' percentage only for entries measured in that survey.23,678 respondents answered the web-framework/technology question; it is multi-select and self-selected.
State of JSKeep its usage/satisfaction values separate from Stack Overflow.State of JS samples the JavaScript community and uses different questions/denominators.
Website market shareUse W3Techs only as detected website technology share and label the snapshot date.Website deployment share is not the same as developer usage, npm downloads, jobs, or framework satisfaction.
Country breakdownDo not infer framework usage from the overall country distribution.A respondent being in a country does not tell us which framework they use; cross-tabs need direct source data.
Gender breakdownLeave per-framework gender data blank unless a survey explicitly supports the cross-tab with sample sizes and all response categories.Inventing male/female percentages would create false demographic precision and discard non-binary/non-response categories.
RankingRank only within a named source and metric, such as Stack Overflow 2025 usage.A universal framework rank would mix incomparable measurements and silently encode editorial preferences.
Historical projectsRetain some legacy frameworks when they are relevant to web history or existing production estates.Educational coverage should explain both modern and legacy stacks without implying equal current adoption.
